sentences.text: The petitioners are the accused 1 and 2 in C.C No.36/2021 on the file of the Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-III (Mobile) Kannur, (Trial Court), which has originated from Crime No.522/2020 registered by the Chakkarakkal Police Station, Kannur, alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 120B r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The petitioners have stated in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case that they have no knowledge of the transfer of the case to the present court and have not received any summons from the Trial Court.

However, the petitioners have reliably learnt that non-bailable warrants have been issued against them, and steps under 2026:KER:20186 CRL.MC NO. 2035 OF 2026 Sections 82 and 83 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have also been initiated against them.
The petitioners are ready and willing to surrender before the Trial Court.
However, the petitioners are apprehensive that their applications may not be considered on the date of surrender and they may be remanded to judicial custody.

I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor On a consideration of the facts and materials on record, without expressing anything on the merits of the matter, I dispose of the Crl.M.C, by permitting the petitioners to surrender before the Trial Court within a week from today and file applications to enlarge them on bail, to recall non-bailable warrant, and the steps initiated under Sections 82 and 83 of the Cr.P.C,, after serving advance copies on the Public Prosecutor.

If such 2026:KER:20186 CRL.MC NO. 2035 OF 2026 applications Suresh Thankappan vs State Of Kerala on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29100026/
2 are filed within the prescribed time period, the Trial Court is directed to consider and dispose the applications, in accordance with law, preferably on the same day the petitioners surrender before the Trial Court.
